slideOverPanel.$description: SlideOverPanel (renamed from Drawer 2026-10-27 — the Storybook name) — a modal panel attached to an edge (right by default, left, or bottom). unlike Popover, blocks interaction with the rest of the page while open (that's what makes it a true dialog, not a floating panel). Uses the native <dialog> element with showModal(): free focus-trap, free Escape-to-close, free ::backdrop, top-layer rendering with no z-index needed. Kept as a token file/build script separate from Modal per explicit prior decision, even though both are '<dialog> with showModal()' underneath — their sizing/positioning/radius differ enough (edge-attached vs. free-floating centered) to earn their own files rather than a shared one with position variants. No outer border — 3 of its 4 edges sit flush against the viewport boundary (no page visible around them to define an edge against), and shadow.md + the backdrop scrim already read as a distinct raised layer; a border would be redundant. radius: none for the same flush-edge reason (Modal, which floats free on all sides, does get one). Three widths for the side placements (2026-10-27): sm 320 (filters, settings), md 480 (a record's detail), lg 640 (dense content, editing); on a phone a side panel leaves a strip of the page visible. Header: title + optional description (Dialog's recipe, resolved from dialog.tokens.json) + an optional header-end slot before the × (a status Badge, a button, a ⋯ menu). Footer is a slot too — any actions, right-aligned. Corners: square on the side placements (three edges sit flush to the screen); the bottom placement rounds its top corners (bottomRadius) — Dialog md/lg/xl take that shape on a phone. Animated open/close via native CSS (@starting-style + transitions on transform/::backdrop, allow-discrete) — no JS animation library. Header and footer are both optional composition, same as Card — a Drawer can be body-only. The close button and footer actions are real interactive elements with their own hover/active/focus states (the same fill.neutral/fill.neutralHover/fill.neutralActive/fill.primary/fill.primaryHover recipe Button itself uses), not unstyled placeholders — anything a user can click deserves real states, doc demo or not. Close (×) is a real Button — ghost, sm, icon-only (32×32, 16px icon) resolved from button.tokens.json — not a component-local recipe; it used to be a hand-sized 28px/18–20px copy of the same ghost colors (changed 2026-09-30).

phoneGutter.$description: 48px of the page left visible beside a side panel on a narrow screen, so it still reads as a layer over the page.

bottomMaxHeight.$description: Bottom placement height cap — literal viewport unit (was a literal in the builder; tokenized 2026-10-26 because Modal md/lg/xl take this placement on a phone).

radius.$description: Square on the side placements — three edges sit flush to the screen, there is nothing for a curve to sit against.

bottomRadius.$description: Top corners of the bottom placement (2026-10-27) — the one free edge; same radius as Dialog, so a Dialog that becomes a bottom panel on a phone keeps its corner. Bottom corners stay square.

padding.$description: 24px — one step more generous than Popover's 16px, proportionate to Drawer being a full modal panel, not a small anchored one.

gap.$description: 12px — internal flex gap within the header row (title-to-close-button) and footer row (button-to-button). Section-to-section spacing (header-to-body, body-to-footer) comes from each section having its own full padding, not from this gap — every section is a full-width band with its own padding.default of 24px, so the divider between them spans the whole drawer width instead of sitting inset (a header/footer border scoped to a single shared-padding wrapper looked wrong once built — a divider that stops short of the edges reads as misaligned on a big edge-attached panel, unlike Card's small inset dividers, which are fine at that scale).

transitionDuration.$description: Literal, not a token — no duration scale exists in this system yet (same 'literal, not invented' precedent as Tooltip's showDelay).

divider.$description: Header/footer section dividers — internal only, the drawer's own outer edge has no border (see $description).
